label: input token e
explanation: Token detector: fires whenever the current input is the letter e (98.5% of e inputs; >99.8% of activations are on e). Fires in both the original and copy phases; never on the delimiter. Magnitude is modulated by phase: copy-phase e inputs (fed-back outputs) activate strongly (~0.65-1.0 of max, all of the top quartile), while original-phase e inputs are weaker (~0.56 of max at t=0, ~0.15-0.45 at later positions). Essentially does not fire on any other token (tiny residual on u, b, g, h).

issues: Minor, systematic but low-impact: most of the 3031 test false positives are original-phase e inputs at t=3-5 that stay below the activation threshold. For (in_tok==e)&(phase==0)&t in {3,4,5}, precision is 0.935 (41081 predicted), compared with 1.000 for copy-phase e and about 0.998 for all other e. The explanation already says original-phase e at later positions fires weakly (0.15-0.45 of max), so this is a magnitude dropout and not a different trigger. It does not depend on digits seen before (precision 0.917 with no prior digits vs 0.960 with at least one) or on in_first. Carving it out would cost a lot of recall (F1 0.890), so no better predicate exists.

The magnitude claims check out. Original-phase steps cover 0% of the top activation quartile, while copy-phase steps cover 100% of the top quartile and 86% of the third. Original-phase t=0 sits in the middle quartiles, which matches its ~0.56 of max.

The selectivity claims check out. The 225 test activations that are not on e hold 0.0% of the activation mass and are mostly copy-phase u at about 0.12-0.14 of max. The feature is active on 98.5% of e inputs, more than 99.8% of active steps are on e, and it never fires at the delimiter step.
Test scores reproduce: precision 0.985, recall 0.999, F1 0.992, mass recall 0.9997.
